sections.text: Rust has two main string types. String is owned text you can grow and change. &str is a borrowed view of some text, like a string literal.
Join strings with format!, which is usually clearer than +:
Strings come with many useful methods:

Rust strings are always valid UTF-8. You can't index a single character with s[0], because a character can take more than one byte. Use s.chars() to walk characters, and s.chars().count() for the character count; len() is bytes.
A good rule: store text in a String, and take &str when a function only needs to read it.
